channel.title: PrintGrams guides
channel.description: Numbers-first guides on 3D printing cost, pricing, electricity and calibration.

item.title: How much does filament shrink? Scale factors by material
item.description: PLA shrinks about 0.2–0.3%, PETG 0.3–0.4%, ABS and ASA 0.5–0.8%, and nylon up to 2%. How to measure your own shrinkage and set the right scale factor in your slicer.

item.title: How long does a 1 kg spool of filament last?
item.description: A 1 kg spool of 1.75 mm PLA holds about 335 m. That's roughly 80 Benchies or 10–20 medium prints. Metres per spool for each material, and how to tell what's left.

item.title: How much filament does a Benchy use? Grams, metres and cost
item.description: A standard 3DBenchy uses about 11–15 g of PLA, or roughly 4–5 m of 1.75 mm filament. Here is how infill, walls and material change that, and what it costs.

item.title: PLA vs PETG: which is cheaper per print?
item.description: PETG is about 2% denser than PLA and often costs the same per spool, so the same part costs only slightly more. Worked examples, cost per metre, and when PETG ends up cheaper.

item.title: How to reduce AMS purge waste on Bambu Lab printers
item.description: Multi-colour prints on an AMS can waste more filament than the model uses. Where the waste comes from, the slicer settings that cut it, and how to work out what it costs.

item.title: Resin vs filament: which costs more per print?
item.description: Resin costs about 1.5–2.5 times as much per gram as PLA, plus alcohol, gloves and FEP film. Worked cost examples for minis and larger parts, and when resin still makes sense.

item.title: What layer height should I use? A practical guide for 0.4 mm nozzles
item.description: Use 0.2 mm for everyday prints, 0.12 mm for detail and 0.28 mm for speed. The 25–75% nozzle rule, how layer height changes print time, and why some printers prefer magic numbers.

item.title: How much electricity does a 3D printer use? Measured figures
item.description: Measured power draw for Bambu Lab, Creality, Prusa, Elegoo and Anycubic printers, why the PSU rating misleads, and what a month of printing really costs in the US, UK, EU and Australia.

item.title: How to calibrate e-steps, rotation distance and flow (Marlin and Klipper)
item.description: The three extruder calibrations that fix under- and over-extrusion, in order, with the exact commands for Marlin and Klipper and the maths behind each one.

item.title: Filament density: why 1 kg of ABS prints more than 1 kg of PETG
item.description: What filament density means, the density of every common material, how slicers use it to turn metres into grams, and how to measure it yourself.

item.title: How much does 3D printing cost? Real numbers for 2026
item.description: What a 3D print actually costs in filament, electricity, printer wear and time, with worked examples for a 20 g keychain, a 150 g phone stand and a 1 kg helmet.

item.title: How to price 3D prints for Etsy, eBay and local sales
item.description: A pricing method that survives marketplace fees: true cost, a fair hourly rate, a margin that reflects design value, and the fee maths that most sellers skip.

item.title: Why your STL imports tiny (or huge): units, scaling and fixing it
item.description: STL files have no units. Here is how slicers guess, why models from inch-based CAD arrive 25.4× too small, how to tell millimetres from inches from the bounding box, and how to rescale without distorting.
